outcomes.text: Use Arabic to discuss time, including clocks, days, months and seasons.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers, gender agreement, number-noun patterns, calendar months and analogue clock times.
Recognise and use Arabic letters in all positions, sun and moon letters, vowel marks, hamza, shadda, sukun, madda and Arabic numerals.
Use ال for definiteness and omit it where Arabic vowel-linking rules require.
Use masculine and feminine nouns, singular, dual, plural, broken plural and idafa constructions.
Use adjective gender, number, position, negation, colours, comparison, demonstratives, nisba forms and common irregular adjectives.
Use common adverbs of time, place and manner, time expressions, adverbial phrases and adverb-plus-noun combinations.
Use subject, possessive, object, prepositional and relative pronouns, including dual and feminine plural forms.
Use common regular, doubled, hollow, weak and irregular verbs in required tenses and time frames.
Form and use past, present, future and imperative verbs, including appropriate negation.
Use perfect and imperfect forms, basic conditionals, subjunctives after common particles and verbal nouns.
Recognise and use passive perfect and imperfect forms, active participles and passive participles.
Use common conjunctions, including forms meaning that, but, because, except, where, then and however.
Use common and less frequent prepositions and connective expressions for location, time, cause and sequence.
Apply Arabic verb-subject-object order and make subjects agree correctly before or after the verb.
Form simple nominal sentences and use إنّ and its related particles, كان and its related verbs, and ليس.
Recognise and use nominative, accusative and genitive case endings.
Express possession with suffixes, including dual and feminine plural forms, idafa, عند and لـ.
Form yes-or-no questions with هل and أ, use أيّ and أيّة correctly, and ask common question-word questions.
Use كم with a singular accusative noun when asking about quantities.
Deduce the meaning of unfamiliar words from context when discussing familiar topics.
Understand and use common adjectives describing qualities, appearance, feelings, size, temperature, condition, value and comparison.
Understand and use common expressions for place, emphasis, quantity, probability, frequency, manner and relationships between people.
Understand and use cardinal, ordinal and fractional numbers, quantities, proportions, totals, frequency and approximate amounts.
Understand and use common verbs for everyday actions, communication, movement, feelings, possession, change, organisation and social interaction.
Understand and use expressions for dates, days, months, years, parts of the day, clock times, duration and sequence.
Learn the months, seasons, dates and related expressions for discussing time and yearly events.
Learn vocabulary for meals and eating routines, including breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks and outdoor meals.
Learn vocabulary for luggage, tickets, vehicles, journeys, passengers, stations, tourists and travel information.
Use expressions for travelling, walking, searching, parking, boarding, leaving, arriving, crossing roads and driving.
Use vocabulary for food and drink, including meals, ingredients, snacks, beverages and utensils.
Learn names of common fruits and vegetables, including apples, oranges, potatoes, tomatoes, onions and mushrooms.
Learn vocabulary for desserts, main courses, healthy food, vegetarian food, starters, meals and snacks.
Discuss the human body, health and illness using appropriate Arabic vocabulary.
Learn vocabulary for major body parts, including the head, limbs, joints, face, organs, skin, throat and fingers.
Use verbs connected with breathing, seeing, smelling and touching.
Learn words for soup, toast, crisps, yoghurt, sandwiches, salad, chocolate, cakes and pizza.
Learn vocabulary for ice, milk, tea, juice, coffee, water and alcoholic or non-alcoholic drinks.
Use verbs and expressions for eating, drinking, feeling hungry or thirsty, preparing food, cutting and becoming full.
Learn vocabulary for rice, tofu, soya, eggs, garlic, cheese, bread, butter, oil, beans, spices, ice cream and pasta.
Learn words for chicken, sausage, fish, meat, beef, lamb, hamburgers and seafood.
Describe food and drinks as hot, sweet, fresh, tasty, salty, raw, cooked or having a particular flavour.
Learn names of cutlery, crockery, cups, pans, glasses, spoons, bowls and other dining utensils.
Learn vocabulary for medicine, clinics, doctors, dentists, nurses, appointments, bandages and medical treatment.
Describe injuries, pain, fever, allergies, colds, headaches, stomach aches, tiredness, vomiting and illness.
Learn vocabulary for sporting activities, equipment, teams, matches, players, scores, medals, winners and sports venues.
Learn names of sports including running, skiing, swimming, gymnastics, golf, rugby, badminton, chess and athletics.
Discuss listening to music, attending events, watching television or films and other leisure activities.
Learn vocabulary for colouring, photography, drawing, fishing, playing instruments, gardening, singing and reading.
Use expressions for taking photographs, sailing, training, drawing sports results, winning, losing, tying and writing.
Communicate about travel and different forms of transport.

topics.title: B1 Self, family and personal relationships

outcomes.text: Discuss oneself, family members and friends.
Describe rooms, furnishings, household equipment and parts of the home.
Discuss clothing and accessories.
Talk about leisure activities, hobbies and sport.
Use greetings, farewells, introductions, thanks, apologies, requests and expressions for asking about wellbeing.
Make, accept or refuse invitations and suggest postponing an activity.
Learn vocabulary for immediate and extended family, relationships, ages, marital status, children, neighbours and relatives.
Use expressions for growing, owning, dying, being born, spelling names, contacting people, raising children and living.
Describe physical appearance using vocabulary for hair, eyes, build, height, age, colour, facial hair, glasses and hearing aids.
Describe personalities and moods using adjectives such as kind, clever, happy, sad, angry, shy, active, calm and amusing.
Express reading interests, affection, crying, hugging, kissing, laughter, smiling, worry and anger.
Use exclamations and interruptions to express welcome, admiration, interest, annoyance, disappointment or surprise.
Learn vocabulary for rooms, furniture and household features such as doors, walls, floors, ceilings, stairs and windows.
Learn bathroom vocabulary including a mirror, toilet, deodorant, comb, toothpaste and towel.
Use verbs for bathing, washing the face, combing hair and cleaning teeth.
Learn bedroom vocabulary including wardrobes, beds, bedding, pillows, lamps and bedrooms.
Use verbs for resting, lying down, waking, feeling sleepy, sleeping and getting out of bed.
Learn living-room vocabulary including sofas, drawers, shelves, carpets, pictures, tables and chairs.
Learn kitchen vocabulary including sinks, bottles, boxes, containers and kitchens.
Use verbs for eating, preparing meals, toasting, sewing, heating, grilling, cooking, boiling, cutting, frying and ironing.
Discuss household chores such as setting tables, baking, taking out rubbish, washing clothes, cleaning, sweeping and tidying.
Learn garden vocabulary including walls, gardens, plants, flowers, fences, trees and grass.
Use expressions for caring for a garden and planting flowers or vegetables.
Learn vocabulary for household appliances and utilities, including electricity, freezers, microwaves, batteries, heating, televisions, radios and refrigerators.
Use verbs for pushing, pulling, switching on or off, repairing and opening or closing appliances.
Learn common colour names, including white, red, green, blue, black, yellow, orange, purple, brown, grey, pink, silver and shades.
Learn vocabulary for clothing and accessories, including trousers, dresses, coats, shoes, bags, jewellery, glasses, scarves and school uniform.
Discuss clothing sizes, formal and informal dress, suitability, tightness, wearing, measuring, putting on and removing clothes.
Discuss educational institutions, learning, training, classrooms, study tools and school subjects.

topics.title: C1 Home town and local area

outcomes.text: Discuss people and places, including continents, countries, nationalities and compass directions.
Learn the names of the continents: Asia, Africa, Antarctica, North America, South America, Europe and Australia.
State a candidate’s or student’s first language, other studied languages, nationality and place of residence.
Describe buildings, services, urban areas and shopping.
Know Arabic vocabulary for buildings and services including schools, farms, hospitals, theatres, offices, libraries, restaurants, hotels, stations and public facilities.
Know Arabic vocabulary for town places, roads, traffic, bridges, squares, markets, neighbourhoods, stations, airports, parks, stadiums and pedestrian areas.
Use Arabic to describe measurements such as size and shape.
Know Arabic terms for measurements including degree, centimetre, gram, kilogram, kilometre, litre, metre and currency exchange.
Know Arabic words describing circles, squares and rectangles, including their corresponding shapes.
Know Arabic vocabulary for size and length, including very small, medium-sized, large, huge, long and short.
Identify and discuss different materials.
Know Arabic vocabulary for materials including plastic, leather, stone, iron, silk, wood, gold, glass, wool, silver, cotton and paper.
Learn the four compass directions: north, south, east and west.
Know Arabic vocabulary for shopping, shops, prices, receipts, bank cards, discounts, cash, customers, supermarkets, butchers and market stalls.
Use Arabic expressions for renting, asking prices, selling, buying, paying, returning purchases, complaining and spending money.
Discuss nature, the environment, climate and weather.
Learn vocabulary for landscapes, natural features, environmental issues and resources, including deforestation, recycling, warming and pollution.
Learn words for climate, regions, scenery, natural resources, stars, rivers, plateaus, air and other environmental features.
Learn names of common animals, including rabbits, lions, snakes, rats, camels, sheep, flies, fish, birds, spiders, elephants, monkeys, cats and dogs.
Learn weather vocabulary for storms, hurricanes, cold, hail, lightning, snow, ice, heat, humidity, thunder, wind, clouds, frost and fog.
Describe weather conditions using expressions for cold weather, heavy rain, rainfall and very hot weather.
Discuss communication, technology, digital life, documents and written texts.
Learn vocabulary for news, information technology, the internet and digital communication.
Know Arabic vocabulary for internet access, information, email, websites, phones, computers, files, applications, social media and online safety.
Use Arabic expressions for going online, clicking, finding, downloading, copying, browsing, calling, uploading, storing, sending and posting.
Know Arabic vocabulary for advertisements, forms, cards, newspapers, passports, notebooks, manuals, letters, certificates, bills, lists, books and magazines.
Discuss jobs, careers and workplaces.
Know Arabic vocabulary for occupations including builders, butchers, soldiers, hairdressers, bakers, firefighters, drivers, postal workers, plumbers, secretaries, police officers and doctors.
Know Arabic vocabulary for dentists, veterinarians, pilots, translators, lawyers, teachers, farmers, flight attendants, nurses, engineers, mechanics, waiters and carpenters.
Know Arabic vocabulary for educational institutions, including nurseries, universities, colleges, primary, preparatory, secondary and private schools.
Know Arabic classroom vocabulary for bells, notebooks, interactive boards, glue, dictionaries, pens, books, rulers, pencil cases, desks, erasers and paper.
Know Arabic names for biology, history, religious education, geography, physical education, mathematics, science, art, physics, chemistry, languages, drama, music and computing.
Know Arabic vocabulary for examinations, instructions, exercises, timetables, lessons, classes, classmates, questions, marks, examples, projects, results, homework and breaks.
Use Arabic expressions for experimenting, answering, studying, taking notes, revising and failing.
Know Arabic vocabulary for businesses, businesspeople, companies, salaries, employers, unemployment, employees, workshops, jobs and professions.
Use Arabic expressions for dismissal, taking leave, retiring, finding, seeking, obtaining or losing employment, receiving promotion and earning money.
Discuss countries, nationalities and languages.

topics.title: E2 Culture, customs, festivals and celebrations

outcomes.text: Discuss culture, customs, faiths and celebrations.
Know Arabic vocabulary for fireworks, baptism, pilgrimage, mosques, circumcision parties, religions, Ramadan, prayers, New Year, public holidays and national occasions.
Know Arabic vocabulary for Eid celebrations, Christmas, Easter, birthdays, Mass, saints, synagogues, churches, temples and private occasions.
Use Arabic expressions for celebrating, giving and believing in something.
